Long Description: As Klara works on her art competition entry, she butts heads with Lucy, feeling misunderstood—and unable to let her mum see her work. Pim feels the same, frustrated that everyone treats him like a baby. When Lucy sends them to the attic to find the Christmas tree, Pim slips and nearly falls through the floor—revealing a hidden courtyard below. With Lucy, they descend via rope ladder, but things get strange fast: Lucy begins regressing in age, soon becoming a younger version of herself—pregnant with Klara. She continues to regress into a teen, passionate about writing. Teen Lucy opens up to Klara, helping her see her mum in a new light. Maybe Lucy does understand her fear of rejection. But as Lucy regresses into a screaming baby, the courtyard darkens. Klara tries to escape, but can’t climb out while holding baby Lucy. Pim, eager to prove himself, climbs out alone and calls Grandma and Grandpa. With their help, they escape—and Klara finds the courage to share her art.
Medium Description: Pim and Klara stumble into a strange and beautiful garden within their own house—and have a wondrous encounter that will forever change the way they see their mum. But can they make it out before it’s too late?
Short Description: Pim and Klara stumble into a strange and beautiful garden within their own house.
Xtra Short Description: Pim and Klara stumble into a strange garden in their home.
Tiny Description: Pim and Klara find a strange garden.

Long Description: In an effort to make ends meet, Lucy announces they’re taking in a boarder. With only two bedrooms, it’ll mean Lucy has to sleep in the kids’ room, much to Klara’s annoyance. She buries herself in her art, working on her entry for the competition, inspired by a postcard from Grandma showing a vast and beautiful landscape. She seeks out Esme, admitting she’s struggling to decide what to enter, but Esme’s reaction leaves her feeling more self-doubt than before. When the boarder arrives, Pim and Lucy are surprised – Eric is a tiny little leaf man. He opts to sleep in the pantry, which he transforms into a bedroom, and obsesses over small objects – bottle lids, lolly wrappers and small plastic blocks. Pim is thrilled, seeing Eric as his new best friend, while Klara shows no interest in meeting him at all. But when Eric goes missing, he panics, believing he’s gone for good. He soon realises Eric isn’t actually missing – he’s with Klara, having gravitated towards her, despite her resistance. He shows her that great art doesn’t have to be about vast landscapes – sometimes tiny details are just as beautiful. Eric leaves without warning, gifting the family a tiny and beautiful garden in the pantry. But the best gift of all is what he leaves behind – a growing sense of family unity.
Medium Description: Klara, Pim and Lucy are feeling disconnected and out of place, but they’re all forced to find a new way of looking at the world, when a mysterious, tiny houseguest comes to stay.
Short Description: Feeling out of place, the family’s world shifts when a strange, tiny houseguest comes to stay.
Xtra Short Description: A tiny visitor helps the family see things differently.
Tiny Description: Lucy rents to a tiny guest.

Long Description: When their cranky neighbour Mrs Katayama breaks Pim’s toy and tosses it back, he’s left dismayed. Lucy sends the kids to the park to cheer him up, and Klara slips away to the Underpass, drawn to the cat-girl, Esme. Meanwhile, Pim meets a strange man in what looks like a space suit, muttering "Karitai" as he wanders the hot streets. Pim decides to help him, and with Klara’s support, they learn he’s not a spaceman but a pearl diver. But what is he searching for? Enter Cat, trying to redeem herself to Klara. She asks Esme to help translate "karitai" – it means "take me home" in Japanese. Opening the diver’s small bag, the kids find a broken toy horse, carefully bound with string. They realise he’s connected to Mrs Katayama. Leading him there, they witness a touching reunion. Later, Mrs Katayama gifts Pim a goldfish, and gives Klara a Daruma Doll, telling her to draw one eye for her wish – and the other when it comes true.
Medium Description: When Pim’s favourite toy is broken by their grumpy neighbor and Mum is too busy to help, Klara takes him to the park to cheer him up. There, they encounter a strange man in what looks like a space suit, who needs their help.
Short Description: While exploring, Pim and Klara come across a curious stranger— one who seems to need their help.
Xtra Short Description: Pim and Klara meet a stranger who needs their help.

Long Description: Klara and Pim join Grandma and Grandpa on a treasure hunt into the barren, mysterious wasteland beyond Outer Suburbia. Each is searching for a treasure with deep personal meaning. Along the way, they’re pursued by a menacing land shark and encounter snapping TVs and mechanical penguins. Klara has a troubling vision of Esme and Cat, stirring her deepest fear—that her bond with Esme isn’t real. Pim has an emotional moment too, believing he sees Dad at the ocean’s edge, only for the vision to vanish. As the land shark closes in, they race to escape, but lose a wheel on their car. While they scramble to fix it, the shark nears. Klara suddenly reaches for Pim’s hand in a show of unity. As they stand together, the shark shrinks and sinks into the sand. In a flash of inspiration, Pim uses Grandma and Grandpa’s wedding rings to secure the spare wheel. The group heads home, tired but triumphant, forever changed by their wild and meaningful adventure.
Medium Description: Klara and Pim go with Grandma and Grandpa on a thrilling treasure hunt, beyond the borders of suburbia. Faced with perplexing challenges, they must decide if they can stick together to find their way home.
Short Description: Klara and Pim join Grandma and Grandpa on a thrilling treasure hunt beyond suburbia.
Xtra Short Description: Klara and Pim face challenges on a treasure hunt beyond subu
Tiny Description: A treasure hunt tests family bonds beyo

Long Description: Feeling the absence of his dad, Pim is desperate for someone to play with, and with Klara too busy, he turns his attention to Lucy, begging her to help him write a story about Dog Boy, who’s looking for his lost dad. Lucy tries to fit it into her already-busy day, and though they get started, the story remains unfinished. On a walk, Pim spots a flyer advertising an art competition, and takes it to Klara, sure she will win with one of her sketches. Klara, however, is consumed by self-doubt, and feels none of her work is good enough. But when a storm blows through, drawing hidden scraps of paper from people’s houses, Klara follows the trail, finding Esme at the underpass as the scraps of paper form a huge ball of discarded poems, pictures and messages in the sky. Esme helps Klara confront her own self-doubt as an artist, and she finally makes a wish, drawing the first eye on the Daruma Doll. She enters the art competition and gets to work on her entry. Meanwhile, Lucy and Pim complete the Dog Boy story – and while it doesn’t result in Dog Boy being reunited with his dad, he finds someone else waiting – Dog Boy’s mum. Pim is delighted with the completed story, and Lucy realises that while she can’t ‘fix’ the fact that the kids’ dad is absent, she is enough.
Medium Description: Budding artist Klara considers braving an art competition, while Pim and Lucy bond by writing stories together. As they all struggle to express themselves, a peculiar storm is brewing in the skies above.
Short Description: Klara preps for an art contest; Pim and Lucy write stories as a strange storm brews overhead.
Xtra Short Description: Klara preps for an art contest as a strange storm brews.
Tiny Description: Klara preps for an art contest.

Long Description: The day of Klara’s art competition arrives, and she nervously heads to the city with Pim. Along the way, Pim panics—what if Klara wins and leaves to pursue life as an artist? Klara reassures him, easing his fears. But at the exhibition, things don’t go as hoped. Klara doesn’t win, and she’s devastated. Feeling like a failure, she destroys her artwork and retreats into sleep, slipping into an inner world that gives her a sudden, deep understanding of the mysterious Sleeping Girl—and her link to Esme and Cat. Pim finds her and gently wakes her. Urgently, Klara hurries to the Twilight house and uncovers proof of the connection between the trio. Moved to help, she uses her artistic gifts to bring the three together in an unexpected and beautiful reconciliation. Back home, Lucy cries tears of joy as she sees Klara’s painting and asks to hang it on the wall. Klara agrees. Later, she draws the second eye on her Daruma Doll—her wish to be an artist has come true, and so has finding her place.
Medium Description: Klara nervously heads to the city for her art competition, with supportive Pim in tow. But when the journey doesn’t go as planned, Klara’s despair leads to a confrontation that will change her—and her neighborhood—forever.
Short Description: Klara heads to the city for her art competition but an unexpected turn shifts everything she knows.
Xtra Short Description: A city trip for Klara’s art leads to the unexpected.
Tiny Description: An art journey takes an unexpected turn.

Long Description: It’s Pim’s birthday, and he’s excited to spend the day with Lucy and Klara, who promise he can do whatever he wants. Pim’s biggest wish is to go to the beach. But Lucy gets an emergency call from work and must postpone their plans. Klara, distracted by her art competition, leaves Pim feeling alone and frustrated. Pim tries to go to the beach by himself, but his plans fail. Returning home, he’s amazed to find himself sitting atop a dugong stranded on their front lawn. Meanwhile, Klara’s creative block swallows her inside a giant Daruma Doll. Esme bravely leaves the Underpass for the first time to help Klara find her artistic courage. Freed, Klara helps Pim care for the dugong and calls wildlife rescue. To their surprise, Lucy arrives—an animal rescuer. Together, they return the dugong to the sea. Pim’s birthday wishes come true with a boat ride, while Klara is struck with new artistic inspiration.
Medium Description: Klara’s self-doubt threatens to swallow her whole, while Pim’s birthday takes a strange turn when a dugong inexplicably appears on the front lawn, far from the ocean and in desperate need of help.
Short Description: Pim’s birthday takes a strange turn when a dugong inexplicably appears on the front lawn.
Xtra Short Description: Pim discovers an unexpected Dugong on the lawn.
Tiny Description: Pim discovers a Dugong on the lawn.

Long Description: Klara and Pim move into a ramshackle house with their mum, Lucy, all struggling to adjust. Klara builds Pim a pillow fort where he feels safe, but the next morning Lucy yells, and Pim runs off, getting lost. While exploring, Klara meets Cat, a confident girl who offers fun and friendship. But Cat’s idea of fun turns to mischief, and she eventually leads Klara to an underpass, where Klara meets Esme – a girl with a cat’s head – who hisses and vanishes. Realising Cat isn’t a real friend, Klara heads home and finds Pim missing. Meanwhile, Pim has discovered a huge Water Buffalo, feeding it pomegranates before falling asleep in a fort of old pillows. Klara finds the fort, but Pim isn’t there – then she realises he’s likely in the pillow fort she made. Sure enough, Pim is found safe. Later, Klara leaves a drawing and apology at the underpass, and is overjoyed when the cat-girl appears in the moonlight, smiling at the gift.
Medium Description: Klara and Pim arrive in their new home, daunted by the upheaval. Klara meets two strange girls—edgy, street-smart Cat and mysterious, reclusive Esme. Meanwhile, Pim runs away and discovers a huge, enigmatic Water Buffalo.
Short Description: Klara meets two strange girls as Pim runs off and finds a giant, mysterious Water Buffalo.
Xtra Short Description: Klara and Pim struggle to adapt to their new home.
Tiny Description: Klara and Pim struggle moving in.

Long Description: With Lucy at work, the kids are left with a list of chores. But Klara is distracted by Tugboat the cat, who leads her to the house across the street—the one always in twilight, where the Sleeping Girl lies. Klara talks to her through the window; the girl remains silent, but Klara is intrigued. Meanwhile, a lonely Pim builds a Dinosaur out of old junk in hopes of making a friend. It magically comes to life, causing chaos and leaving a trail of destruction. The kids scramble to clean up the mess. They dismantle the dinosaur and create a new "friend"—inspired by the only person who could possibly fix things: their mum. Junk Mum springs to life, zooming through the house, tidying and repairing everything just in time. When Lucy gets home, she’s amazed by how clean and orderly things are, believing the kids did it themselves. She's thrilled—and Klara and Pim are left with a new appreciation for everything their mum does.
Medium Description: With Klara enthralled by an intriguing neighbour and Lucy starting a new job, Pim needs someone to play with. He builds a dinosaur friend out of junk, stunned when it comes to life. But their fun quickly gets out of hand.
Short Description: With Klara distracted, Pim builds a junk dinosaur—only to watch it come wildly to life.
Xtra Short Description: Pim builds a junk dino that comes to life and causes chaos.
Tiny Description: A dinosaur comes alive and runs wild.

Long Description: Pim is thrilled when the day of his annual father-son fishing trip arrives—until Lucy breaks the news: Dad isn’t coming. Heartbroken, Pim shuts Lucy out, and nothing she does can reach him. Desperate, Lucy calls Grandpa for help. Grandpa arrives with mysterious fishing gear and takes Pim up to the roof, where they cast their lines into the sky. Luminous skyfish circle above, and Pim catches a rare moonfish. He’s overjoyed—until the fish dies, and grief sets in. But Grandpa reveals they’ve harvested the moonfish’s eggs. Together, they launch them skyward, watching as they hatch into hundreds of glowing baby moonfish. Meanwhile, the news about Dad hits Klara just as hard. She shuts down, avoiding Lucy, Grandma—even Esme. But Grandma gently helps her through the grief, offering space and understanding. Slowly, Klara realises that sharing her feelings is far healthier than bottling them up—and that she’s not alone in missing him.
Medium Description: Pim grapples with big feelings about his absent dad, so Grandpa takes him sky-fishing to lift his spirits. Meanwhile Grandma helps Klara realise she can no longer deny her own overwhelming emotions.
Short Description: Pim goes sky-fishing with Grandpa to cheer up while Grandma helps Klara process grief.
Xtra Short Description: Pim & Klara grapple with big feelings for their absent dad.
Tiny Description: Pim & Klara deal with big feelings.
